question: A customer asks to return items from three separate orders. Your coordinator agent spawns one subagent per order, and each subagent calls lookup_order. When any subagent fails, the coordinator currently ends the whole case and sends the customer a generic apology, even when the other two checks succeeded. A teammate proposes that subagents catch every lookup_order failure and return an empty order record marked as success, so that cases never stop. Which changes should the team make?

options.text: Adopt the teammate's proposal, so that the coordinator always receives a successful response and completes every return without stopping the case for a lookup failure.
options.reason: Returning empty results as success silently suppresses errors, which is an anti-pattern. The coordinator would then treat a failed lookup as an order with no data.

options.text: Keep ending the whole case on any failure, but first rerun all three subagents from the start once so that a transient lookup error has a second chance.
options.reason: The workflow still ends completely because of a single failure, which is an anti-pattern. Rerunning the subagents that succeeded also wastes their valid results.

options.text: Have a failed subagent report the failure type, the lookup it attempted and any partial results instead of returning a success response.
options.reason: Silent suppression is an anti-pattern. Structured error context such as the failure type, the attempted query and the partial results lets the coordinator make a recovery decision.

options.text: Let the coordinator finish the two orders whose checks succeeded and handle only the failed order through a retry or a targeted escalation.
options.reason: Ending a whole workflow because of one failure is an anti-pattern. It discards valid partial results. The coordinator should continue and recover only the failed part.

options.text: Have a failed subagent return a short generic status such as 'order lookup unavailable' so that the coordinator can move on without extra detail about the failure.
options.reason: A generic error status hides the failure type, the attempted query and the partial results. The coordinator then cannot choose an appropriate recovery.
